labels.title: Semantic labels
labels.about: A CLIP model compares rendered views of the whole drawing and of each stroke group with the words of a vocabulary and names the best matches. Models trained on photographs often struggle with abstract line drawings.

description.about: A vision-language model that runs on the server PC looks at rendered views of the drawing and describes what it sees. It is told not to interpret the person.

summary.title: Conclusion by a language model
summary.about: A language model that runs on the server PC writes a short summary from the measurements, the indicators and the other AI findings of this drawing. The template summary above stays the default text.
summary.hint: A language model can say things that are not in the data. Check every statement against the measurements and the drawing.

settings.title: AI settings
settings.subtitle: Which AI functions are on, which models they use, and the rule base and vocabulary that steer them.
settings.principles: All AI runs on the server PC. No drawing data leaves it, nothing is sent to a cloud service, and only free models are used. AI output is decision support for the psychologist, never a diagnosis.
settings.functionsHint: Every function can be switched off on its own.
settings.allOff: AI is switched off completely in the server configuration.
settings.evaluationHint: A function counts as evaluated once it was tried on a sample set of drawings together with a psychologist and the agreement and the failure modes were written down.
settings.switchHint: The switches and the evaluation flags are set in the server’s config.py and are read when the server starts.
settings.modelsHint: Every model and library with its version, licence and status. A model is only downloaded when you start it here.
settings.licenceUncheckedLong: The licence is recorded from the publisher’s model card. It has not yet been checked against the use in the study.
settings.downloadBody: This downloads {{size}} onto the server PC. It runs in the background.
settings.rulesHint: The rules behind the indicators, with the reason for each rule.
settings.rulesInvalid: The rule base file {{file}} is invalid, so the indicators are off:
settings.rulesEdit: The rule base is a text file on the server. Edit it there; a change takes effect without a restart. Change “status” to “reviewed” only after psychologists reviewed the rules.
settings.vocabularyHint: The words a CLIP model can choose between. A word that is not here can never be an answer.
settings.vocabularyOther: Amber entries are “other” entries (scribble, pattern, almost empty): they let the model say that nothing recognisable is there.

flags.legacySchema: Saved by an older version of the game (data version 1): some data is missing.
flags.thinnedTracking: The body tracking was thinned out to fit the storage limit, so tracking-based results are approximate.
flags.fewStrokes: Very few strokes: the statistics are hardly meaningful.
flags.allErased: All strokes were erased: nothing is left to analyse.
flags.missingFigurePosition: The position of the figure is missing, so the distance to the figure cannot be computed.
flags.missingTimeData: No time information: the time and speed results are unavailable.
flags.multipleSittings: The drawing was continued after a break of more than 30 minutes: the time results only count the time spent drawing.

metricReasons.noTimeData: The drawing has no usable time information.
metricReasons.noPressure: Saved before the trigger pressure was recorded.
metricReasons.noFigurePosition: The figure position is not stored with this drawing yet.
metricReasons.noChromaticInk: Only grey, black or white ink was used.
metricReasons.noInk: The strokes have no length, so there is no ink to measure.
metricReasons.noEvents: Saved by a game version that did not record events.

strokesDrawn.name: Strokes drawn
strokesDrawn.definition: Number of strokes that are still part of the drawing.
strokesDrawn.note: A stroke is one continuous line, from pressing to releasing the trigger.

strokesErased.name: Strokes erased
strokesErased.definition: Number of strokes that were drawn and then erased.
strokesErased.note: Erased strokes stay in the data. They are analysed as behaviour, not as part of the drawing.

pointCount.name: Points
pointCount.definition: Number of sampled points of the drawn strokes.
pointCount.note: Depends on the drawing speed and the sampling rate, so it says little about detail by itself.

totalLength.name: Total length
totalLength.definition: Summed length of all drawn strokes, in metres of the game world.
totalLength.note: It reflects how much was drawn, more is not better.

meanStrokeLength.name: Mean stroke length
meanStrokeLength.definition: Total length divided by the number of drawn strokes.
meanStrokeLength.note: Short strokes can mean a careful, detailed way of drawing or hesitation. Look at the drawing as well.

boundingVolume.name: Used space
boundingVolume.definition: Volume of the box that contains all drawn strokes.
boundingVolume.note: Shows how much space was used. One stray stroke makes the box larger (outlier trimming is planned).

heightRange.name: Height range
heightRange.definition: Difference between the highest and the lowest point of the drawing.
heightRange.note: Depends on how far the participant can reach.

figureDistance.name: Distance to the figure
figureDistance.definition: Mean distance of the drawn points from the figure shown in the scene.
figureDistance.note: Needs the figure position, which is not stored with the drawings yet.

drawingSpan.name: Time span
drawingSpan.definition: Time from the start of the first stroke to the end of the last stroke.
drawingSpan.note: Includes the pauses between strokes, but not breaks of more than 30 minutes (the drawing was continued later).

activeTime.name: Active drawing time
activeTime.definition: Time during which at least one stroke was being drawn.
activeTime.note: The pauses between strokes are not included. With several authors, simultaneous drawing counts once.

idleTime.name: Pause time
idleTime.definition: Total length of the pauses between strokes that are longer than the pause limit (5 s).
idleTime.note: Long pauses can mean thinking, hesitation or distraction. Pauses are only seen between strokes, so they say nothing about what the participant was doing. Breaks of more than 30 minutes are not pauses.

meanSpeed.name: Mean speed
meanSpeed.definition: Total length divided by the active drawing time.
meanSpeed.note: Slow can mean careful or hesitant, fast can mean confident or hurried. It only describes.

directionalChange.name: Directional change
directionalChange.definition: Mean turning angle between consecutive segments of the strokes, from 0 (straight) to 1 (turning back).
directionalChange.note: Natural curves count too. High values come from many changes of direction, for example tremor, scribbling or tight curves. The definition is still under review.

meanPressure.name: Mean trigger pressure
meanPressure.definition: Mean value of the controller trigger while drawing, from 0 to 1.
meanPressure.note: Only drawings saved by newer versions of the game have it.

leftHandShare.name: Left-hand share
leftHandShare.definition: Share of the drawn strokes that were drawn with the left hand.
leftHandShare.note: Compare with the dominant hand of the participant.

warmShare.name: Warm colours
warmShare.definition: Share of the coloured ink that is warm (red, orange, yellow, pink).
warmShare.note: Grey, black and white ink is not counted. The meaning of colours differs between people, so treat it as a description.

distinctColours.name: Distinct colours
distinctColours.definition: Number of clearly different colours, each with at least 2 % of the ink.

eraseRatio.name: Erased strokes
eraseRatio.definition: Share of all strokes that were erased.
eraseRatio.note: Can reflect self-correction. Interpret it together with the drawing.

menuOpens.name: Menu opens
menuOpens.definition: Number of times the participant opened the in-game menu.
menuOpens.note: Only drawings saved by newer versions of the game record this.

toolChanges.name: Tool changes
toolChanges.definition: Number of changes of the drawing mode, colour or width.
toolChanges.note: Frequent changes can reflect exploring the tools or searching for the right one. Only newer drawings record this.

roadmap.decisionsHint: The scope decisions of requirements.md that shape this prototype.

decisions.SC-01: Every psychologist sees every session, drawing and participant.
decisions.SC-02: No changes to the existing database model, only the new tables of Phase 3.
decisions.SC-03: The analysis is an additive server module that only reads the existing data.
decisions.SC-04: The active session stays global, as it is now.
decisions.SC-05: English UI, all texts in translation files so Hungarian can be added.
decisions.SC-06: Real names are shown, no consent flags. Feedback is the exception.
decisions.SC-08: Phase 3 only adds tables, an admin role value, a sign-up check and request throttling.
decisions.SC-09: The admin sees feedback pseudonymously, never who sent it.

roadmap.futureHint: Ideas that need database, server or game changes, so they are not requirements now.

future.FUT-01: Session ownership, sharing and a reduced Browse level
future.FUT-02: Parallel psychologists: an active session per psychologist
future.FUT-03: Drawing revision and creation time in the database
future.FUT-04: Persistent store for analysis results and reports
future.FUT-07: Pseudonyms, anonymised export, audit log, consent flags
future.FUT-08: Paginated list endpoints and a light drawing endpoint
future.FUT-09: Store the figure position in the drawing
future.FUT-10: In-game camera snapshots at save time
future.FUT-14: Saved views and feedback on AI insights
future.FUT-18: Admin user management and audit log
future.FUT-19: Data rights and retention for submissions
future.FUT-20: Submissions attached to sessions, drawings or reports
